title: DSC — Discite Computatrum Scientia
subtitle: Computer science education that doesn't need a computer.

sections.heading: The Why
sections.content: There are millions of children in rural communities with little or no technology access who will never touch a computer in a classroom. But computational thinking — decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithms — doesn't need a screen. It needs a teacher who knows how to play the right games. DSC is a curriculum of unplugged activities: board games, card games, group challenges, storytelling, and physical movement. No computers required, every concept sticks. Because these learners aren't being prepared to survive the digital world as passive consumers — they're being prepared to shape it as innovators and problem solvers.

sections.heading: The Vision
sections.content: Years ago I wrote that every child should learn computer science, not to become a programmer, but to become a creator — someone who understands the logic behind the tools they use, rather than just consuming whatever tech hands them. That philosophy hasn't aged a day. DSC is the practical manifestation of that idea: a full lesson plan series built for the reality of rural classrooms where a teacher's creativity matters more than a computer lab budget. Revived in 2026 with a sharper scope: two pillars — computational thinking (decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithms) and programming as a mindset, taught without a single computer — for middle school through high school, in classrooms where the only technology is a teacher's creativity. The world these learners are growing into is increasingly digital; the point is that they meet it as innovators and problem solvers, not as passive consumers.

sections.heading: What's Coming
sections.content: lesson plans that a teacher can pick up and run with in 30 minutes, no training needed
items: The Programming Course — 18 unplugged lessons (half a school year) teaching the skeleton every language shares: variables, conditionals, loops, functions, debugging. Lessons 1 and 2 are written and ready to teach; the rest are being drafted right now
A Magic Forest board game that teaches sequencing and conditionals through storytelling
Complete Grade 1 and Grade R term plans mapped to the SA CAPS curriculum
Teacher training materials — because the best unplugged lesson falls flat if the facilitator isn't confident
Assessment frameworks that measure computational thinking without a written test
A community contribution model so other educators can adapt and share their own lessons

sections.heading: Stay Tuned
sections.content: I'm rebuilding, updating, and expanding this project from the ground up. Six years of new ideas, deeper understanding of how kids learn, and — honestly — a much better sense of what actually works in a real classroom. The early materials were promising. The next iteration is going to be something I'm genuinely proud to put my name on.
